l.i: ut vinea Naboth Achabo, fel in ore ipsorum, putredo Nomini, tinea familiis, & conscientia-rum aculeus.
Divide eorum linguas[?] & corda, qui sic invicem fœderantur contra Ecclesiam, & Regnum: ut insipientia eorum manifesta fiat omnibus, & ultra non proficiant.
Sed propitius esto Iustitiæ mcæ[?] (Domine) ut in misericordia Altissimi non commovear.

page.notes: The running head is Greek and is transcribed in Greek letters. The first paragraph's "familiis" is followed by a mark that may be a comma or a ꝫ; I have read it as a comma before "&". "linguas" has an ink blot over part of the word. "mcæ" appears to lack a letter (probably meæ) and is printed as seen. "commovear" is printed as seen; it may be a printing error for "commoveat".
